They want homes that support wellness, foster a sense of community and make everyday routines feel more effortless,” shared Hans Lopez-Vito, head of Brand Experience and Brand Strategy for Residential, Estates, and Corporate at Ayala Land. “At Park Central Towers, we designed the residences, amenities, retail environment, and hospitality together because we believe they should work as one living ecosystem rather than as separate components,” he continued. Space of modern living Designed by internationally acclaimed Singapore-based Soo Chan Design Associates in collaboration with Leandro V. Locsin Partners, Park Central Towers balances density with openness. Roughly half of the 1.5-hectare estate remains dedicated to open spaces, while nearly 10,000 sqm. have been allocated exclusively for resident amenities. Another 10,300 sqm. comprise Park Central Plaza, the development's retail component that complements everyday living without compromising residential privacy. The South Tower rises 70 floors with 281 residences, while the 56-story North Tower houses 259 units. Residences range from expansive two-bedroom homes to four-bedroom units and signature Anadem residences measuring above 1,000 sqm. Equally notable is the low-density planning. With only five to six residences per floor, homeowners enjoy a greater sense of exclusivity rarely found in vertical developments. Lifestyle amenities occupy the three-level podium, featuring a concierge, swimming pool, fitness center, multipurpose court, social hall, boardrooms, indoor and outdoor play areas, game room, lounge, veranda, and even a dedicated pet training yard. Sky Terraces are also carved into each tower to provide additional gathering spaces, wellness areas, outdoor lounges, and panoramic views of the city skyline. Below, Park Central Plaza transforms the ground plane into an extension of residents' daily routines. Soon, establishments such as Wolfgang's Steakhouse, One World Deli, Hojicha Café, Enka by Hapag, Casa Bertazzoni, Eluvo Health, GAOC Dental, and Lunchbreak Beauty will create a neighborhood where dining, wellness, and lifestyle conveniences are only an elevator ride away. A life of possibilities Perhaps the most defining element of Park Central Towers is how it adapts to individual lifestyles. Residences offer flexible spaces that homeowners can convert into additional bedrooms, home offices, hobby rooms, or wellness spaces depending on changing needs. Premium appliances are also integrated into the residences, while select homes feature dramatic double-height ceilings that further enhance the sense of openness. The project likewise marks Ayala Land's first branded residences integrated with Ayala Land Hospitality. This introduces hotel-inspired services rarely found in residential developments, including an in-house general manager, concierge assistance, housekeeping, laundry services, fitness trainers, pet grooming coordination, restaurant reservations, private chef services, yacht experiences, and even chartered helicopter and private jet arrangements. For Paloma Urquijo Zobel de Ayala, creative director of Ayala Land, luxury is ultimately remembered through experiences rather than possessions. "When we were developing Park Central Towers, we wanted people to build a relationship with the building over time. That's why the artworks aren't presented as a collection to be viewed all at once—they're encountered naturally as part of everyday life,” she said. “Hospitality follows the same idea. It isn't defined by grand gestures, but by thoughtful moments that make people feel welcomed, understood, and at home. Those experiences give a residence its warmth and its character." That philosophy extends to one of the property's most distinctive features—its art program. Working with Tarzeer Pictures, Ayala Land Premier commissioned more than 40 contemporary Filipino artists, integrating their works throughout hallways, lounges, and shared spaces instead of confining them to a traditional gallery. Residents discover the collection gradually as they move through the building, creating a more personal relationship with both the art and the spaces they inhabit. More than decorative pieces, the artworks become part of everyday life, reinforcing the idea that luxury is found not only in grand statements but also in meaningful moments. Park Central Towers ultimately represents more than another premium residential address in Makati. It reflects how luxury living continues to evolve where architecture, hospitality, wellness, culture, and placemaking come together to create homes designed not only for today, but for the years ahead.

FIFA defends Infantino against allegations tied to his time at UEFA. LONDON (AP) — FIFA has issued a statement defending its president, Gianni Infantino, against what it calls a “concerted and ongoing effort” to undermine his leadership of the organization. The statement was released Saturday, Aug. 8, a day after a report by British newspaper The Daily Telegraph raising questions about an exit package paid by UEFA to a female staffer who worked with Infantino when he was general secretary of European soccer’s governing body. UEFA confirmed that a “departure payment” was made to the employee and said it was “in line” with regulations at the time. Infantino worked at UEFA for 16 years before being elected FIFA president. In the statement Saturday, FIFA accused Infantino’s critics of trying to weaken his authority and remove him from office without due process. “It is increasingly evident that there is a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine FIFA and its president,” the FIFA statement said. “Those who do not have the support of FIFA’s member associations should not seek to achieve through allegation, insinuation or misinformation what they cannot achieve through FIFA’s established democratic processes.” It said some reporting has included “unsubstantiated assertions and demonstrably false claims” which shouldn't be presented as fact. “Change inevitably challenges established interests, but disagreement with that change cannot justify efforts to undermine the democratic mandate of FIFA’s president or the institution he was elected to lead.” Infantino faced intense backlash after details of his plan to sell World Cup profits to private equity were published. UEFA and two other continental confederations — North America’s CONCACAF and the Asian Football Confederation — rejected the plan. He did receive backing from FIFA’s management board last Wednesday following a meeting in Morocco, and he apologized over the process. UEFA’s threat to have its 55 member countries boycott FIFA competitions until the plan was scrapped remained, with UEFA saying Thursday that the announcement “changes nothing.” While confirming the exit payment “was in line with the regulations that existed for departing staff at the time,” UEFA said the rules had been tightened since 2016 and currently “reflect those found in a modern, high-profile organization.”

Jorge Messi, Lionel Messi’s father and longtime agent, dies at 68. ROSARIO, Argentina (AP) — Jorge Messi, the father of soccer star and Argentina captain Lionel Messi, died Saturday, Aug. 8, at a hospital in the central Argentina city of Rosario. He was 68. The Rosario-based Club Atlético Newell’s Old Boys announced his death in a social media post that said he had undergone treatment in recent months for an unspecified illness. The post described him as “the pillar and the person who, with vision, rigor and affection, supported the career of the best player of all time, alongside his wife, Celia Cuccittini.” The South American Football Confederation, CONMEBOL, in a statement also offered its condolences “with respect and affection for Lionel.” Lionel Messi led Argentina to a runner-up finish in this year's World Cup. In the team's first match, against Algeria, he was visibly emotional after scoring the first of his three goals. He said later that he wept for “a reason unrelated to sports.” “I went through some difficult, complicated days,” he said. “I am grateful to the delegation, to all my teammates, because they were always by my side wishing me strength so that I would be OK.” Media reports at the time outraged the Messi family, which days later released a statement confirming that “Jorge is experiencing a health issue,” without specifying the nature of his condition. “A person’s health and the peace of mind of their loved ones should not be the subject of speculation or irresponsible media interest,” according to the statement, which also expressed “discomfort at the lack of sensitivity, respect and scruples with which some people have treated a strictly private and family matter.” Jorge Messi was a chemical technician and worked as a steelworker. He played soccer as a midfielder and reached the youth ranks of Newell’s Old Boys but had to abandon the sport to complete his mandatory military service in Argentina. He played a fundamental role in his third son’s career, serving as his agent and managing his business affairs. He was the one who traveled with a young Messi to Barcelona in the early 2000s for the trial that would open the doors to La Masia, the club’s youth academy. Lionel Messi made his professional debut in 2005 and went on to win eight Ballon d’Or awards. He led Argentina to the 2022 World Cup title. “My dad was always by my side,” Lionel Messi said in a 2007 interview with Radio del Plata. “Sometimes I would lock myself in my room to cry when we arrived in Barcelona, or my dad would do the same without me seeing him, or thinking I didn’t see him. We pretended we were both OK, but we weren’t. My dad even asked me what I wanted to do when we were feeling down, if I wanted to stay or go back, and I wanted to stay, and he stayed with me.” His father negotiated the contracts with Barça and later his transfers to Paris Saint-Germain and Inter Miami, while also managing the use of his famous son’s image rights and his numerous investments in real estate, hotels, and restaurants. In 2013, father and son were accused by a Spanish prosecutor of trying to conceal earnings from the player's image rights. Jorge Messi paid more than than 5 million euros ($6.6 million) on Aug. 14 to cover alleged back taxes and interest. In Rosario, a sign at the VIP Rosario restaurant, one of the Messi family’s gastronomic ventures, indicated that it was closed for the day. The president of Argentina's soccer federation, Claudio Tapia, on Saturday issued a lengthy statement in which he recognized Jorge Messi “for having raised a person of values: humble, respectful, and deeply committed to others.” The organization ordered a moment of silence to be observed at all matches across all categories of Argentine soccer and mandated that players, referees and coaching staff wear black armbands.

More cops, PNP assets mobilized as heavy rains continue. Gen. Jose Melencio C. Nartatez, Jr., chief of the Philippine National Police (PNP), ordered the mobilization of additional personnel and equipment for disaster response as Metro Manila and most part of Luzon and the Visayas are expected to be continuously pounded with heavy rains. This means that the threat of widespread flooding remains, as well as other damaging effects that include landslides road and bridge damage. Nartatez said police commanders in areas affected by the weather disturbance were tasked to assist local government units (LGUs) in ensuring public safety, particularly on evacuation and other disaster response. Nartatez said police personnel are continuously coordinating with the LGUs and other concerned agencies for strategic deployment in areas where manpower and equipment are needed for rescue operations and other disaster response. More police assets and other resources have also been placed on standby to assist communities affected by heavy rains and strong winds. “Our personnel and our resources have been closely monitoring and conducting real-time response in coordination with the LGUs and other frontline services. We made available as many personnel and resources for evacuation and other disaster response,” said Nartatez. Heavy rains brought by weather disturbances prompted the Philippine Atmospheric Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) to raise rainfall warnings over Metro Manila and other provinces several times since Friday. Intense rains will continue to batter parts of Luzon and the Visayas through Tuesday, Aug. 11, as two tropical cyclones outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) enhance the southwest monsoon or “habagat.” The rains, ranging from 50mm to 200mm, are expected to continue until Tuesday. Nartatez said local police units will remain in close coordination with local authorities as weather conditions develop. He said police personnel are prepared to respond to residents who may need assistance or evacuation. Nartatez urged the public to monitor weather developments and follow official instructions from local authorities, “We urge the public to remain calm but vigilant and heed the advice of authorities for your own safety.”

Bianca Umali, Ruru Madrid spend weekend together after cheating confession goes viral. After making headlines with his confession that he cheated on Bianca Umali, Ruru Madrid appeared to put the controversy aside as he and Bianca spent the weekend together on a road trip. Bianca posted a glimpse of their road trip in an Instagram post on Saturday, Aug. 8. “Sponty road trips are the best with the bestie!” Bianca wrote in her caption. The post came days after Ruru’s cheating confession went viral, prompting a wave of comments on both their Instagram accounts. Despite the renewed attention, Bianca’s post showed the couple seemingly carrying on with their weekend as usual. During his “Fast Talk with Boy Abunda” appearance, Ruru was asked about his previous statement that cheaters can change. Looking back on the mistake he made, the actor took accountability and said he remains grateful that Bianca eventually gave him another chance. “Siguro ’yon ’yong pinagpapasalamat ko kay Bianca na kahit po nagkamali ako during that time. I was 20 years old at hindi ko naman po sinasabing dahilan ’yong pagkabata sa ginawa kong pagkakamali, pero siguro itinuturing ko rin siyang blessing in disguise somehow,” Ruru said. Ruru also said their temporary breakup made him realize just how important Bianca was to him. “Dahil from there, nakita ko po talaga ang kahalagahan ni Bianca. Nag-break kami ng 8 months but now 8 years na po kami. Tinanggap niya ako ulit. Kasi ang Diyos nga natin marunong magpatawad. At ’yong cheating choice talaga siya,” he added. Ruru and Bianca began dating in 2018 but publicly confirmed their relationship in 2022.

2nd alarm raised in Marikina River due to 'habagat'; Monday classes suspended. The Marikina City government raised the second alarm at the Marikina River on Sunday morning, August 9, after the water level reached 16 meters due to continued heavy rains brought by the enhanced southwest monsoon (habagat). The Marikina City Rescue 161 raised the first alarm at 8:44 p.m. on Saturday, Aug. 8, after the river’s water level reached 15 meters. It remained on the first alarm until Sunday morning before the water level reached 16 meters at 10:56 a.m., prompting authorities to raise it to the second alarm. According to the city’s early warning system, residents in low-lying areas, especially those near the river, are advised to voluntarily evacuate to designated evacuation sites following the raising of the second alarm. A third alarm will be raised once the river’s water level reaches 18 meters, prompting the implementation of forced evacuation protocols in all affected areas. On Saturday night, Mayor Maan Teodoro ordered the opening of the city’s main evacuation centers to prepare for the immediate evacuation of residents if necessary. Rescue boats, ambulances, and other emergency assets have also been deployed in various parts of the city to ensure a swift response in case of flooding. The city government continues to monitor weather conditions, the water level of the Marikina River, and the situation in flood-prone areas. It also urged residents to remain alert and follow advisories from authorities. The local government also suspended classes at all levels in both public and private schools on Monday, Aug. 10, due to the expected continued rains. 'Maleta boys' just 'pawns', must name their 'king'--quad-comm boys. The members of the 18 "maleta boys" who retracted their affidavit have betrayed their role as "pawns", thus they must now reveal who their "king" is. Remarks from Manila 6th district Rep. Bienvenido "Benny" Abante Jr. and former Surigao del Norte 2nd district Rep. Robert Ace Barbers point to this demand as authorities try to decide on what to do with the recantation of at least four of the controversial bodyguards-slash-flood control projects mess bagmen. “Their recantations clearly show that someone prepared a script and used them to spread false allegations against senior government officials and members of the House prosecution panel,” Barbers said, as he described them as mere "pawns" in the situation. The former overall chairman of the House quad-committee (quad-comm) was referring to the solon-prosecutors who are out to get a conviction on Vice President Sara Duterte in her ongoing Senate impeachment trial. Barbers is serving as House impeachment adviser. Asked whether the recantations strengthened the House prosecution panel’s credibility, he said yes. "Ang pagbawi ay nagpapakita na may nagdikta at nag-udyok sa kanila na mag-sinungaling, at ito ay isang sadyang pag-atake para siraan ang impeachment process. Malamang konsensya at napakong pangako ang dahilan ng pagbawi nila," he noted. (The retraction shows that someone dictated and pushed them to lie, and this is a deliberate attack meant to discredit the impeachment process. Most likely conscience and broken promises are the reasons for their retraction.) According to reports, Rosebert Macasasa Waupan, Cecilio Serafica Larroder Jr., Benny Bulontate and Bernard Tube — who identified themselves as former bodyguards of former Ako Bicol party-list Rep. Zaldy Co — executed separate affidavits withdrawing statements they had previously submitted to the Office of the Ombudsman. Mention names Abante, the current quad-comm overall chairman--challenged the four maleta boys who walked back on their previous remarks to identify the persons allegedly behind the preparation of supposedly fabricated affidavits. He said the recantations raise serious questions that must be answered, particularly after the four alleged that they had been pressured, threatened or induced into signing prepared affidavits. “Ang hinihingi natin ay simple: buong katotohanan. Kung fabricated ang mga affidavit, sino ang nag-fabricate? Kung scripted, sino ang gumawa ng script? Kung may mastermind, pangalanan at patunayan,” Abante said. (What we are asking for is simple: the whole truth. If the affidavits are fabricated, who fabricated them? If they are scripted, who wrote the script? If there is a mastermind, name and prove it.) Their previous sworn statements contained allegations against President Marcos, former House Speaker Martin Romualdez, Co, and several other political personalities. They also claimed that lawyer Levito Baligod was among those who allegedly directed their activities and coached them on their public statements. “If they are now saying that their previous affidavits were fabricated, then they have a responsibility to identify the people behind them. Name names, tell the whole story, and present the evidence,” added Abante, who last February endorsed an impeachment complaint against Vice President Duterte. Abante stressed that a recantation by itself does not settle the issue of what is true or false. He said the new allegations of fabrication, coercion and inducement must likewise be subjected to scrutiny and supported by evidence. Abante earlier filed libel and cyberlibel complaints against Baligod and 18 former bodyguards after he was implicated in allegations involving supposed deliveries of cash-filled luggage.

Arrest of all Taguig's most wanted for July hailed as PNP steps up drive vs fugitives. Authorities arrested the 10 most wanted persons in Taguig City for the month of July, the way the Philippine National Police (PNP) wants it to be when it ordered all police commanders to regularly update its wanted list as part of the renewed efforts against fugitives. PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio C. Nartatez, Jr. earlier explained that the accounting of wanted persons is itself a crime prevention measure since a number of them were involved in at least two more criminal activities. He also tasked police commanders to regularly update the arrest warrants. In the case of Taguig, those arrested are facing various cases that include rape, acts of lasciviousness and child abuse, as well as violations involving illegal drugs and falsification of public documents. Taguig Chief of Police Col. Julius Añonuevo said the arrests were carried out through sustained intelligence gathering, surveillance and the implementation of outstanding warrants. He said the accomplishment demonstrates the persistence of police personnel in locating wanted persons and enforcing court-issued warrants, and the support of the local government unit, particularly Mayor Lani Cayetano. "Every warrant served is the result of determined police work. We will continue to track down wanted persons, carry out our duties professionally and help ensure that cases against them proceed through the justice system,” said Añonuevo. In separate anti-drug operations, police seized a combined 201.39 grams of suspected shabu worth about ₱1.37 million, including a ₱1.02-million haul from a high-value individual along C6 Road. Taguig police also identified a woman whose body was found inside a suitcase in Barangay Tanyag and arrested three individuals after investigators traced the case to a suspected crime scene and recovered evidence that helped establish her identity and the circumstances surrounding her death. In another high-profile case, police arrested a suspect positively identified in connection with the viral gunpoint robbery of an online seller, recovering a firearm and a hand grenade during the operation.

OCD: 382,000 people affected as fishermen rescued, hundreds evacuated amid torrential rains. The combined effects of the enhanced southwest monsoon (habagat) and previous tropical cyclones “Luis” and “Maymay” have affected around 382,000 people in eight regions as heavy rains triggered flooding, landslides, and dangerous sea conditions. The Office of Civil Defense (OCD) said the affected population, equivalent to 110,000 families, were recorded in Cordillera Administrative Region (CAR), Ilocos (Region 1), Cagayan Valley (Region 2), Central Luzon (Region 3), Calabarzon (Region 4A), Mimaropa (Region 4B), Bicol (Region 5), and Zamboanga Peninsula (Region 9). Of the number, about 2,200 families or 7,300 people were staying inside 86 evacuation centers in the affected areas while 1,132 families or 3,700 people were staying outside evacuation centers. The death toll remained at six while seven others were injured in incidents linked to the weather disturbances but OCD information officer Diego Mariano said the figures were still subject to validation. Meanwhile, no missing persons were reported as of 6 a.m. Rescue efforts As the rains continued, the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) also carried out rescue and evacuation operations in communities affected by flooding and rough seas. In Laoag City, Ilocos Norte, two fishermen were rescued after their motorbanca capsized off Barangay 32-B La Paz on Aug. 8. The fishermen were fishing in the area when their motorbanca encountered large waves and capsized, according to the PCG. Personnel of the Coast Guard Sub-Station Laoag City, assisted by local residents, reached the fishermen using a bamboo raft until both fishermen were brought safely ashore and were reported to be in good condition. The fishermen were later turned over to the City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office for medical assessment. PCG Commandant Admiral Ronnie Gil L. Gavan commended the Coast Guard Sub-Station Laoag City personnel and the local residents who helped in the rescue. On land, the Coast Guard Station Cavite and Coast Guard Outpost Imus evacuated about 102 residents affected by severe flooding in Imus City, Cavite. In Nasugbu, Batangas, the PCG Sub-Station Nasugbu also evacuated 87 residents from Sitio Sampaguita, Barangay Calayo, after flooding hit the area. Another 50 residents were evacuated in Barangay Libjo, Batangas City, by the PCG and the City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office. They were brought to Libjo Elementary School, which served as a temporary evacuation center. The PCG said it remained alert in flood-prone and landslide-prone areas and urged residents to cooperate with authorities and follow safety advisories. Additionally, sea travel was also disrupted by the weather as the PCG Command Center monitored 215 stranded passengers, 105 rolling cargoes and eight stranded vessels in 22 affected ports from 4 a.m. to 8 a.m. Sunday. The affected ports were under the Coast Guard districts of Western Visayas, Bicol, Southern Tagalog and Central Visayas. Damage The flooding and landslides also added to the damage already recorded by the OCD. A total of 148 houses were damaged, of which, 138 were partially damaged while 10 were totally destroyed. Infrastructure damage was estimated at P105.5 million while agricultural losses reached P3.53 million. The government and its partners had provided P13.21 million worth of assistance to affected families, according to the OCD.

Dustin Yu, Bianca de Vera ride wave of rising popularity into 'Ba’t Di Na Lang Tayo'. No doubt, Dustin Yu and Bianca de Vera are among today’s hottest showbiz tickets. Their sold-out fans day, “DustBia: Love Actually,” is proof of that, with tons of devoted fans gathering at the venue, screaming their names hoarse and getting giddy over practically everything they said or did. It is quite a sight for two young stars whose rise has happened in such a short time. Indeed, it seems like only yesterday when they first started making hearts swoon during their stint on “Pinoy Big Brother.” It could have ended as quickly as it began, as is often the case with reality-show pairings, but the fans would not let it. They followed Bianca and Dustin from one project to the next, giving DustBia a life beyond the “PBB” house. Now, here we are. As announced during the same fans day, the two are set to star in a movie titled “Ba’t Di Na Lang Tayo” under Regal Entertainment, a production house familiar to generations of moviegoers for creating hit vehicles for the popular love teams of their time, dating back to the 1980s. With that comes a different set of expectations. There are more people watching now, and considerably more riding on what they do next. For two young performers still learning the business, it would be easy to be overwhelmed by the speed of it all. Bianca does not seem to see it that way. “I think pressure is a good thing because that just means patuloy yung hunger namin,” she told us. “Personally naniniwala ako na when the day comes na hindi na’ko gutom, I feel that would be such a great disappointment to me, the younger version of myself who was once so hungry and was once so passionate about what she’s doing,” she said. “So I want to be hungry hanggang sa makakaya ko.” Dustin, meanwhile, has Bianca to go through it with. “Buti na lang talaga na may kasama ako ngayon sa career ko, na tumutulong sa akin na hindi muna magpahinga,” he said. The two have taken to discussing their plans, the things they still need to learn and what they can improve as a love team. “Nagfo-focus kasi kami ni Bianca sa goal namin, which is to make more projects together,” Dustin said. “Talagang inaaral namin bawat bagay na kelangan namin matutunan. Pinag-uusapan namin mga plano, mga kelangang pa naming iimprove as love team.” Bianca puts it more simply. “Masaya rin ako kase this time around meron akong nakakasama, meron akong kakampi, meron akong kadamay,” she said. It is easy to appreciate the sense of perspective in the way the two talk about their careers. They know they have been given a chance, and they seem intent on making the most of it. They are young, they have the looks and they have the chemistry that made audiences take notice in the first place. But there is also an evident willingness to learn the business and put in the work. That brings them to “Ba’t Di Na Lang Tayo.” The film follows two young people dealing with the responsibilities of adulting, with romance developing as they try to make sense of this new stage of their lives. But as responsibilities mount and life takes its inevitable turns, they are left to find out whether love can keep pace. There is a bit of irony in that. Bianca and Dustin are young themselves, figuring out what comes next as their careers move at a pace neither probably expected when they first entered the “PBB” house. “Yeah, may mga similarities pero may mga differences din sa pagkatao namin in real life,” Dustin said. Bianca agreed, adding, “Like Dustin said, hindi 100 percent. And that’s where the acting comes in.” But what about the fans who helped bring them to where they are now? Does the need to keep them happy ever weigh on them? “Minsan, I couldn’t help but feel that need to please them, make them happy,” Dustin said. “But at the end of the day, I just hope they allow enough room to grow.” Director Jason Paul Laxamana, for his part, is not about to let the DustBia phenomenon dictate the film. “Yung skill nila talaga, yun ang mahalaga. Na-obserbahan ko na sila dati pa, at yun ang dahilan kung bakit excited ako makatrabaho sila,” he said. That may be the more interesting part of the DustBia story. The fandom has already established their appeal, and the two have shown that there is talent behind the pretty faces. Now comes the box office. For two young actors at the start of what could be a long career, it is another chance to see how far they can go.

Solon files bill increasing tax exemption on taxable income to P500,000. ‎TACLOBAN CITY — Southern Leyte second district Rep. Christophershon Yap has filed a bill increasing the tax exemption on taxable income to P500,000. ‎ House Bill 10505 aims to amend the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended, by imposing a zero percent tax rate for individual taxpayers earning below P500,000. ‎ For income over P500,000 but less than P800,000, a 15 percent tax applies on the amount exceeding P500,000; for income over P800,000 but less than P2 million, P45,000 plus 20 percent of the amount exceeding P800,000; for income over P2 million but less than P8 million, P285,000 plus 25 percent of the amount exceeding P2 million; and for income over P8 million, P1,785,000 plus the excess over P8 million. ‎ Married individuals shall compute their individual income taxes separately based on their respective total taxable incomes. ‎ If any income cannot be clearly attributed or identified as earned or realized solely by one spouse, it shall be divided equally between them for tax purposes. ‎ Minimum wage earners will continue to be exempt from income tax on their taxable income. Their holiday pay, overtime pay, night shift differential, and hazard pay will also remain tax-exempt. ‎ Self-employed individuals and or professionals may opt to pay an eight percent tax on gross sales, gross receipts, and other non-operating income exceeding P500,000, in place of the graduated income tax rates specified in the Tax Code.

Rayco, Olaguir find groove as Alas Girls down Tunisia for win No. 2 in FIVB worlds. SAN FELIPE, Chile—Alas Pilipinas is finding its rhythm just as Xyz Rayco and Resty Olaguir are rediscovering their groove, taking another step toward the Round of 16 with a 27-25, 25-19, 25-16 rout of Tunisia on Saturday, Aug. 8, in the FIVB Volleyball Girls U17 World Championship. Key players in the Alas Pilipinas Girls squad that earned the berth in this world meet through the Asian Women’s U16 Championship last year in Jordan, Rayco and OIaguir revived their old connection and pushed the Philippine team to a 2-1 win-loss record. After an opening loss to defending champion China, world No. 25 Alas Pilipinas has taken down higher-ranked foes in succession, downing No. 8 Mexico before sweeping No. 20 Tunisia at Liceo Particular Mixto San Felipe. That put Alas Pilipinas in second spot in Pool B, behind only defending champion China, with two playdates left in the preliminaries. The top four advance to the Round of 16. With Olaguir running the offense, Rayco found the openings that had eluded her in the first two matches of the team supported by the Philippine Olympic Committee, Philippine Sports Commission and Asics. “It feels different when she sets ne the ball, it feels like I can really kill it,” Rayco said. “Of course, I’ll work hard to be able to play my best whoever I share the court with.” The 16-year-old Rayco, top offensive threat in the Asian U16 meet in Jordan, finished with 13 points on 12 attacks and a block, including two of Alas Pilipinas’ final three points to seal the nerve-racking first set. “I’m happy because everyone contributed. I’m also happy with my game because I was able to show how I really play. I’m satisfied even though I made mistakes because I was able to bounce back and show who I am as a player,” Rayco said. “The past two days, I didn’t feel like I was playing the right way. I felt like I played poorly. My teammates said it was fine, but I wasn’t satisfied, so today I really wanted to bounce back. I’ll keep this going.” Olaguir said she didn’t expect to be fielded with Irish Mahinay running the offense, but the Ateneo setter settled in when Alas hit a shaky stretch in the opening set. “I’m happy I got in and contributed. I think I’m slowly getting back to the way I really play” Olaguir said. “There are still a lot of things I need to work on. I hope this continues and that I don’t llet my emotions get the better of me.” Caera Celis continued her stellar play and wound up as Alas Pilipinas top scorer for the third straight match, delivering 15 points on 13 attacks and two blocks. Sharina Rhyza Lleses came up with 10 points, all from attacks, for the Philippines, which returns to action after the tournament break on Sunday as it battles world No. 6 Peru on Monday and end up pool play against No. 12 Venezuela on Tuesday. Gabriela Ayala Torres scored 15 to lead Tunisia, while Isabella Gallardo Sibara, had points for Mexico.

Fil-Chinese seniors vie in ASEAN cagefest. The Filipino-Chinese Veterans Basketball Association (FCVBA) is out to re-stamp its class when it vies in the ASEAN Seniors Basketball Tournament starting on Tuesday, Aug. 11, in Kuching, Malaysia. With the inclusion of former PBA stars Elmer Reyes, Aries Franco, and Benjie Poblete, the FCVBA Bearcats are confident of taking the 70 years division title back after losing to ZAAP of Bangkok last year. Other members of the team are Rain or Shine co-team owner Terry Que, Ironcon Builders’ Jimi Lim, Eduard Tio, Danny Ching, Andrew Ongteco, Julio Cruz, Amang Santos, James Chua, Med Sultan and Achit Kaw. Former Adamson player Chingka Lee will be calling the shots for the team determined to restore the country’s pride in the event long dominated by Fil-Chinese seniors. “With Reyes and Franco around, I think we have a good chance of winning the title again,” said Que, one of the team’s godfathers – the others are Lim and Tio. FCVBA will also competing in the premier 50-year’s division for the first time in a long while, with former Ateneo star Jean Alabanza, team captain Edster Sy, Dexter Quan and Oliver Choa leading the team. Though the 50-years squad is not a deep as before coach Willy Chan believes they can their rivals a run for their money. Completing the 50-years cast supported by ITG/Triangle Tires are Kerby Chua, Kenneth Lim, Calvin Li, Francis Sy, Edwin Herrera, Edwin Yap, and Sherwin Yao.

Lovely Abella, emotional after scammers used her identity to dupe people. Lovely Abella-Manalo became emotional as she called out scammers using her identity to deceive people and collect money. The actress posted an emotional video on Facebook to warn the public about it while appealing to those behind the fake accounts to stop victimizing others. "Napakasakit, biktima din po ako ng mga scammer, ginagamit ang video ko, ginagamit ang photo ko para makapangscam sila, madaming nag aakala na ako yun dahil video ko yun," Lovely wrote on her caption. According to Lovely, the scammers re-uploaded her videos, created fake pages, and use forged certificates to deceive buyers. They also threaten customers and use AI-edited videos to advertise fake jewelry prices. She added that the scammers may have a courier accomplice. Lovely reminded customers that her business accepts payments only through bank transactions, not cash on delivery. Despite the frustration of seeing her identity being used to deceive others, Lovely said she continues to pray for the people behind the scam. "Kahit saan kalat na ang mukha ko pero kay LORD ako nagsusumbong, na sana hawakan niya ang puso ng mga scammer ?” Lovely then urged the scammers to stop deceiving people. "Maawa po kayo sa mga nabibiktima ninyo, sana magkaron kayo ng takot sa DIYOS sa mga ginagawa ninyo. ??? Masarap po magkaron ng pera na galing sa Panginoon hindi sa Demonyo!!! Wag po kayo magpalinlang, wag niyo po sirain ang integridad ninyo para sa PERA!! Magtrabaho po kayo ng patas!! ???,” she ended. Lovely has repeatedly warned followers about fake accounts. She advised customers to deal only with her verified social media pages and official bank accounts.

Fil-Chinese alumni cagefest resumes with GCC out to keep title. (FCAAI) starting on Monday, Aug. 10, at the Tanduay gym in Quiapo, Manila. Coming off a successful staging of the premier age category – the 40-above – league chairman Wilbert Loa sees another spirited race for the title, which the Graceans won via a two-game sweep of St. Stephen’s High School in the inaugural staging of the event last year. “We are praying that we’ll have a good weather tomorrow,” said Loa, who is looking forward to another round of exciting games just like the previous divisions. Fireworks, BYD Valenzuela, BAIC, Jetour, Yong Kee Roasting House, 1118 Autospa, and TCL.

San Fernando, Pampanga suspends classes Monday due to severe weather. ‎ ‎SAN FERNANDO CITY, Pampanga — Face-to-face classes on all levels here are suspended on Monday, Aug. 10, due to severe weather, the city government announced Sunday. ‎ Mayor Vilma Balle-Caluag ordered the suspension following PAGASA’s 11 a.m. heavy rainfall warning on Sunday, which placed Pampanga under a red warning level. ‎ The City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office said the effects of the enhanced southwest monsoon or "habagat" may continue through Monday. ‎ Schools may shift to online learning or other alternative delivery modes to ensure continuity of education. ‎ School administrators were asked to consider the situation of learners, particularly those living in flood-prone areas. ‎ The city government reported flooding in several areas, with some roads already impassable to light vehicles. ‎

Libanan to future health workers: 'Compassion trumps AI'. House Minority Leader 4Ps Party-list Rep. Marcelino "Nonoy" Libanan has reminded the country’s future health workers that compassion is of their greatest strengths in an ever-evolving world. Libanan recently delivered a speech before graduating students and academic awardees at the University of the Philippines (UP) Manila School of Health Sciences’ System-Wide Recognition Rites, held under the theme “50 Years of Service, Social Accountability and Solidarity," at the Philippine International Convention Center (PICC). “Compassion is your biggest weapon against artificial intelligence (AI),” Libanan said, referring to the irreplaceable human ability to care, understand, and comfort others. Quoting Albert Schweitzer, the ranking solon told the graduating students: "Everyone must work to live, but the purpose of life is to serve and to show compassion and the will to help others.” Libanan says true education is not only about academic achievement but also about shaping character and giving hope to others. He recalled the influence of his mother, Pacita, who was both a parent and a teacher in his life, and how he witnessed her dedication in preparing lessons, understanding her students, and finding joy in their success. “Doon ko po natutunan na ang tunay na edukasyon ay hindi lamang tungkol sa mga grado o diploma. Ito po ay tungkol sa paghubog ng pagkatao at pagbibigay ng pag-asa sa kapwa,” Libanan said. (That is where I learned that true education is not only about grades or diplomas. It is about shaping character and giving hope to others.) Personal connection Libanan also shared his personal connection to the healthcare profession, recalling that before studying law and entering public service, he was a Medical Technology student. He said his training taught him the importance of discipline, patience, and respect for every member of the healthcare team. “Sa larangan ng kalusugan, wala pong maliit na detalye. Ang bawat resulta ng laboratoryo ay maaaring maging batayan ng isang desisyong magliligtas ng buhay,” said the minority leader. (In the field of health, no detail is small. Every laboratory result can be the basis of a decision that saves a life.) “Sa likod po ng bawat specimen ay isang tao—isang pamilyang naghihintay ng magandang balita, isang batang umaasang gagaling, o isang mahal sa buhay na ipinagdarasal ng kanyang pamilya,” he added. (Behind every specimen is a person—a family waiting for good news, a child hoping to recover, or a loved one being prayed for by their family.) The minority leader also honored the UP Manila School of Health Sciences for five decades of fulfilling its mission of providing quality health education to communities that need it most. “For 50 years, this institution has done more than produce graduates. It has formed men and women who understand that knowledge carries with it a responsibility to serve, particularly those living in underserved and marginalized communities,” Libanan said.

Delivery rider dies after being struck by toppled tree, post in Antipolo. A delivery rider who was taking shelter along Circumferential Road in Barangay San Roque, Antipolo City, died after being struck by a toppled tree and post on Sunday, Aug. 9, amid continued rains brought by the southwest monsoon (Habagat). Mayor Jun Ynares said the rider was immediately brought to the Rizal Provincial Hospital System Antipolo Annex 2 for medical treatment, but was later pronounced dead. The incident occurred at Simeon Compound, in front of Clean Fuel in Grand Heights, Barangay San Roque. Ynares said the city government will assist the rider’s family in bringing his remains home from the hospital and will help them with the necessary arrangements for his wake and burial. Motorists were advised to avoid the area and use alternative routes while clearing operations are underway. “Patuloy ang clearing operations para maalis ang mga nakaharang at maibalik sa normal ang daloy ng trapiko (Clearing operations are ongoing to remove the obstructions and restore normal traffic flow),” he said. The mayor added that high rainfall volumes have also been recorded at various rainfall stations over the past week. As of 12 p.m. on Sunday, the following rainfall totals were recorded over the past 24 hours: •Antipolo (Capitol) station – 127.0 mm •Bagong Nayon (COGEO) – 152.5 mm •Bosoboso – 143.0 mm He therefore reminded residents, especially those living in low-lying and flood-prone areas, to exercise caution, as the soil may have become saturated and unstable after days of rain, potentially causing soil erosion and landslides in mountainous and elevated areas. The local government said it continues to monitor the situation together with the barangays. Residents were advised to remain alert and immediately report any hazardous conditions in their areas.

Eala eyes quarters berth vs former champion Bencic in Toronto. Alex Eala faces another formidable rival in world no. 14 Belinda Bencic in the for a spot in the quarterfinals of the National Bank Open in Toronto, Canada on Monday, Aug. 10 (Philippine time). Match is set not earlier than 8:10 a.m. (PH time) with the 25th-seeded Eala seeking to ride the momentum of her hard-fought third-round victory over American Caty McNally, 6-3, 5-7, 6-4. The 12th-seeded Bencic, who won this WTA 1000 tournament back in 2015, is also coming off a tough match of her own, bouncing back from a first-set stumble to turn back Taylor Townsend, 6-7 (5), 7-6 (4), 6-4. The thrilling showdown marks the first time that Eala and Bencic are facing each other, with the 29-year-old Swiss star bringing an imposing resume that includes winning the gold medal at the 2020 Tokyo Olympics and having twice reached the Grand Slam semifinals. The former world No. 4 also won 10 WTA Tour singles titles and two in doubles. Last year, she rose from No. 421 to No. 11 in the world rankings during her first full season back on tour after taking a maternity leave. This year, she is equally imposing, winning a mixed doubles title at Indian Wells, making into the quarterfinals of the Miami Open, and fourth-round finishes at the French Open and the Wimbledon. Eala is equally impressive, having won her breakthrough WTA Tour title at last week’s Mubadala DC Open and riding on a seven-game winning streak since then. She also reached a historic fourth round at Wimbledon. A win over Bencic would match Eala’s best WTA 1000 finish of the season -- a quarterfinal run at the Dubai Tennis Championships last February. It would also set up a quarters meeting with the winner between Alina Korneeva and fourth seed Coco Gauff.

‎Dagupan folk told to stay on alert as flood persists. ‎DAGUPAN CITY -- Mayor Belen Fernandez urged people here to stay alert as several barangays and major roads remain affected by flooding due to continued rains from the southwest monsoon. ‎ Fernandez said the Sinucalan River has reached 7.50 meters above sea level (MASL), or above critical level, raising concerns over further flooding in low-lying communities. ‎ The mayor stressed that Dagupan, being downstream, continues to receive water from upstream areas. ‎ She also said the gates of Ambuklao and Binga dams in Benguet are open for water release, while San Roque Dam in Agno, Pangasinan remains under monitoring. Residents in flood-prone areas were urged to remain vigilant, secure important belongings, and prepare for possible evacuation if water levels continue to rise. The city government, barangays, and frontline response teams remain on alert to assist affected communities. ‎ “Alam kong nakakapagod na (It is already tiring),” Fernandez said, acknowledging the difficulty faced by residents from the situation. ‎ ‎ ‎

2,424 classrooms damaged by ‘habagat’ rains—DepEd. At least 2,424 classrooms across several regions were damaged by the recent southwest monsoon or “habagat” rains, the Department of Education (DepEd) said on Sunday, Aug. 9. “Initial assessments from the DepEd Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Service (DRRMS) as of August 9 show a total of 2,424 damaged classrooms across affected regions, comprising 403 totally damaged, 505 with major damage, and 1,516 with minor damage,” the agency said in a statement. According to the education department, its regional and schools division offices are currently validating data to identify priority areas for the immediate deployment of personnel who will help clean up affected schools. DepEd said it is working with the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) to expand their joint response and speed up the recovery of public schools damaged by habagat. The agencies will use their 2026 Tulong Panghanapbuhay sa Ating Disadvantaged Workers (TUPAD)-Brigada Eskwela convergence as an immediate disaster cleanup mechanism to help restore affected classrooms. DepEd Secretary Sonny Angara thanked DOLE, led by Labor Secretary Francis Tolentino, and the Office of the Executive Secretary (OES), headed by Executive Secretary Ralph Recto, for providing manpower and operational support for school readiness and emergency cleanup efforts. The agency said that as of July 30, DOLE had funded the deployment of 168,517 temporary workers across 9,186 public schools nationwide under the TUPAD-Brigada Eskwela initiative. The program provided P1.07 billion in financial assistance to support school opening operations, according to DepEd. As such, Angara lauded DOLE for its commitment to provide emergency labor assistance to habagat-affected schools. “Ngayong hinaharap natin ang pinsala ng habagat, muli tayong nagpapasalamat sa DOLE sa kanilang mabilis na pagtugon (As we deal with the damage caused by the habagat, we once again thank DOLE for its swift response),” he said. “Sa tulong ng ating emergency labor augmentation, mas mabilis nating malilinis at maipapaayos ang ating mga silid-aralan upang maiwasan ang anumang abala sa pag-aaral ng ating mga kabataan (With the help of our emergency labor augmentation, we can clean and repair our classrooms more quickly to avoid any disruption to the education of our youth),” he went on.

Stray Kids unclear on Grammy plans after BTS boycott. Stray Kids decliined to address questions relating to the Grammys, this, after BTS' decision not to submit an entry to next year's awards created noise. According to a report from the Korean Herald, the K-pop group repeatedly dodged the question insisting they're focused simply on creating good muisc. "We've never once set out to make an album chasing a particular award or record. When we talk about the music or performances we love, it doesn't come from how we're seen from the outside — it comes from what's inside us as we build a stage or write lyrics. It's less about outside expectations around awards and more about capturing the sound and story we want to tell," Seungmin said. Asked directly about the Grammy's newly added Best Asian Pop Music Performance category , Seungmin stopped short of addressing whether Stray Kids would submit an entry. "I feel so thankful that K-pop, as a genre, is loved this much around the world. It makes me realize all over again just how powerful music can be," he said. Hyunjin echoed the group's long-held approach. "Throughout our time as Stray Kids, we've never once set our sights on a particular award or achievement when releasing an album. With this album, too, what we want most is to show and prove that we can do 'this and that' — anything and everything. That's really our biggest goal and dream. Above all, we want our fans to be satisfied and happy," Hyujin added. It can be recalled that BTS’ decision not to submit an entry for the Grammys has fueled debate over the Recording Academy’s new Best Asian Pop Music Performance category for the 2027 awards.

PH lifters reap more medals in Tashkent tilt. Five more Filipino lifters added to Team Philippines’ medal haul after posting podium finishes in their respective divisions at the 2026 Asian Youth & Junior Weightlifting Championships in Tashkent, Uzbekistan on Saturday, Aug. 8. Jerick Icon Castro, Kirby Kent Alas-as, Prince Kiel Delos Santos, Alexsandra Ann Diaz and Angeline Colonia combined for eight gold, five silver and four bronze medals, further boosting the team’s medal tally after just two days of competition. The 15-year-old Diaz, niece of Philippines’ first Olympic gold medalist Hidilyn Diaz-Naranjo, dominated the youth women’s 49kg division with hauling three gold medals in snatch (77 kg), clean & jerk (92 kg) and total (169 kg). The world youth record-holder also competed in the junior women’s 49 kg, where she finished bronze in snatch (77 kg) and total (169 kg). Angeline Colonia also saw action in the junior women’s 49 kg, topping the snatch with 80 kg, but finishing with silver in clean & jerk (93 kg) and total (173 kg) behind eventual winner Naruemol Vonghajak of Thailand. Castro and Alas-as also shared the podium in the men’s youth 60 kg. Castro swept all three gold medals in snatch (116 kg), clean & jerk (144 kg) and total (260 kg), while Alas-as bagged the bronze in snatch (110 kg) and total (243 kg). Also making a mark was Delos Santos in the junior men’s 60 kg, where he ruled the snatch (120 kg), and finished with the bronze in clean & jerk (144 kg) and total (264 kg). Althea Bacaro and Jay-R Colonia delivered the early medal haul for the Nationals with two gold medals, while Colonia won two silvers and a bronze. Also competing in the tournament are world youth champion Albert Ian Delos Santos (men’s 70kg), junior bets Jhodie Peralta (women’s 53kg), Rosalinda Faustino (women’s 57kg) and Mango Prince David Tarro (men’s 65kg), and youth team members Jea Mae Palagtiw (women’s 69kg) and Rhianne Cabalida (women’s 77kg).

LIST: Flooded roads, hazards reported in Metro Manila on Aug. 9. Flooding persisted in multiple parts of the capital by Sunday afternoon, Aug. 9, as continuous rains from the southwest monsoon (habagat), enhanced by Tropical Depression “Maymay,” inundated key roads and low-lying communities. As of 2:02 p.m., the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) reported gutter-deep to half-gutter-deep flooding along several sections of Taft Avenue, including Quirino Avenue, Escoda Street, and the NBI/United Nations area, though all remained passable to all types of vehicles. The Manila City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Department (MCDRRMD) earlier flagged a wider list of flooded areas across the city, including Taft Avenue (NBI, PGH, Pedro Gil, and Vito Cruz), United Nations Avenue, Padre Faura, Roxas Boulevard service road, España Boulevard, Blumentritt, and areas near the Manila North Cemetery. Floodwaters reached up to one foot in parts of Taft Avenue, corner General Malvar, and España Boulevard, corner Antipolo Street, while several other roads experienced gutter-deep flooding. A fallen tree also struck a vehicle along Lacson Avenue late Saturday night near the Laon Laan–Dimasalang intersection. No injuries were reported, and clearing operations were immediately carried out, allowing traffic to resume. In Sta. Mesa, particularly Barangay 598 along Likha Street near the San Juan River, authorities continued close monitoring after continuous overnight rains, with the situation reported stable as of 10:00 a.m. Elsewhere in Metro Manila, flooding was also reported in Mandaluyong, where F. Ortigas Avenue corner Boni Avenue remained gutter-deep but passable, and in Quezon City, where floodwaters reached about three inches along Araneta Avenue in Barangay Tatalon past noon. In Makati, clearing operations continued along EDSA after a subdivision wall collapsed a day earlier due to the rains. The weather disturbance also triggered evacuations and emergencies in several areas. In Marikina, around 1,900 residents have been evacuated to various centers as water levels are being monitored. In Muntinlupa, at least 31 families (132 individuals) were displaced and brought to evacuation centers in Barangays Putatan and Tunasan, as well as Bagong Silang Elementary School. Authorities are closely monitoring lakeside communities, with Laguna Lake’s water level at 11.68 meters, still below the critical 12.5-meter mark. In Taguig, a landslide struck Medel Extension in Barangay Central Signal, forcing the evacuation of one family while four others were being assisted. Emergency responders were deployed, and aid was provided to affected residents. PAGASA said the habagat, intensified by the tropical depression, continues to bring prolonged rainfall over Metro Manila, raising the risk of further flooding. Authorities remain on high alert, with rescue teams on standby and residents in flood-prone areas urged to stay vigilant, avoid inundated roads, and follow evacuation advisories as rains persist.

Philippines bars Middle East, European animal imports after FMD outbreaks. The Department of Agriculture (DA) has suspended imports of live animals and selected animal products from seven economies in the Middle East and Europe following confirmed outbreaks of foot-and-mouth disease (FMD). Signed by Agriculture Secretary Francisco P. Tiu Laurel Jr. under Department Circular No. 39, the emergency ban aims to protect the domestic livestock industry from the highly contagious viral disease. The restriction covers shipments originating from Azerbaijan, Bahrain, Cyprus, Iraq, Israel, Kuwait, and Palestine. The Philippines imports virtually no live animals or fresh meat directly from these seven economies, sourcing the bulk of its supply from Brazil, the United States (US), and Spain. Under the order, the government has banned the entry of live swine, cattle, water buffaloes, and other susceptible species. The suspension also extends to fresh skeletal muscle meat, animal casings, tallow, hooves, horns, and bovine semen. The measure follows an official notification from the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) confirming localized outbreaks of the FMD virus serotype SAT1. The findings were validated through laboratory testing coordinated by the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) reference network. To enforce the ban at the border, veterinary quarantine officers at all Philippine ports of entry have been ordered to immediately intercept and confiscate non-compliant shipments. The DA clarified that commodities classified as safe under international veterinary standards will still be permitted, provided importers present valid sanitary certifications. Allowed goods include ultra-high-temperature (UHT) processed milk, dairy products, heat-treated canned meat, protein meal, gelatin, and specific processed hides and leather. Foot-and-mouth disease affects cloven-hoofed animals such as pigs, cattle, sheep, goats, and buffaloes. While it poses no health risk to humans or food safety concerns, uncontained outbreaks can devastate livestock production, cause local supply shortages, drive up farmgate production costs, and inflict severe economic losses on agricultural producers. “The Philippines has worked hard to protect its livestock sector from devastating animal diseases,” Tiu Laurel said in a statement. “Acting swiftly against emerging risks is essential to safeguarding food security, protecting farmers' livelihoods, and preserving public confidence in our food supply.” He emphasized that Manila is maintaining a science-based, precautionary stance—prioritizing the health of the domestic agricultural economy while remaining open to safe international trade.

Hunter Biden says his father's prostate cancer has spread and is causing him pain. LONDON (AP) — Former U.S. President Joe Biden ’s prostate cancer has spread to other parts of his body and is causing him pain, even as he continues to speak out on public issues, his son Hunter said in an interview. In a wide-ranging interview with the BBC broadcast late on Friday, Hunter Biden grew emotional as he discussed his father’s condition, describing it as very sad to watch. “The cancer has spread, metastasized into his bones and further," he said. "It’s very painful and it's very debilitating in many respects.” Joe Biden, 83, was the oldest man to serve as U.S. president and his age was a source of concern for much of his four years in office. He and his White House advisers have faced intense criticism for allegedly concealing the extent of his problems, especially after he was forced to abandon his bid for re-election after a disastrous debate with his eventual successor, Donald Trump. The former president revealed his cancer diagnosis in May of last year, less than four months after he left the White House. Hunter Biden said the diagnosis had been tough on the family. “It's really sad to watch," Biden said. “The only thing that I'd say about my dad, about his health right now, is I wish he would complain more, because it’s not good.” But Biden said his father remains “out there," speaking publicly about the issues that are important to him. “He’s still doing his thing," he said. “He so believes in this country." The former president will publish a memoir, “Promise Me, America,” after the mid-term elections.

Shanghai cancels 1,300 flights as China prepares for Typhoon Dolphin. BEIJING (AP) — Shanghai's two airports canceled more than 1,300 flights and authorities relocated some 300,000 people in surrounding regions as China prepared for Typhoon Dolphin, after the storm brought heavy rains to northern Taiwan. The outer bands of the storm on Saturday hit northern Taiwan, including the capital Taipei, bringing rain. Some Taiwanese airlines also canceled their flights to China Sunday. The storm’s maximum sustained winds were estimated at about 162 kilometers per hour (101 mph) as of Sunday morning. It is bringing heavy rains, creating a risk of severe flooding as well as landslides and is expected to hit Zhejiang province and northern parts of neighboring Fujian province late Sunday. Forecasters in China predicted that areas could see 200-400 mm (7.9–15.7 inches) of rainfall over the next few days. Authorities are warning of severe landslide risks in Zhejiang. Shanghai's Hongqiao and Pudong airports respectively also canceled about 60% of Sunday's expected flights, according to the Paper, Shanghai's state media. On Saturday evening, authorities in Zhejiang evacuated some 390,000 people in the city of Taizhou. Authorities in Shanghai evacuated some 30,000 plus from riskier areas. Schoeman, Van Coevorde defy odds to conquer IRONMAN 70.3 Lapu-Lapu. LAPU-LAPU CITY – Henri Schoeman rediscovered his winning form in Cebu, overcoming punishing heat, a choppy swim and a blustery bike course before fighting through cramps in the closing run to reclaim the men’s professional crown at the IRONMAN 70.3 Lapu-Lapu here on Sunday, Aug. 9. The 34-year-old South African clocked 4:08:52 over the demanding 1.9-km swim, 90-km bike and 21-km run course, returning to the top two years after his breakthrough triumph in the same race presented by Megaworld. He won his first Lapu-Lapu 70.3 in 2024 in 4:02:31, beating another deep international field. But this victory carried far more weight for Schoeman, who has endured two difficult years trying to regain the form that once made him one of the world’s elite triathletes. “This win means so much, you know. I've had a really tough two years, struggling to find my form,” said Schoeman, who described the victory as a major confidence boost and a sign that there is still more to come. Schoeman said the race largely unfolded according to plan, with the swim setting up his decisive move on the bike. He pushed hard in the opening leg before creating the gap he needed on the 90-km ride, which again featured the imposing Cebu-Cordova Link Expressway (CCLEX). The bike, however, was no easy ride even for the world-class professionals. Strong winds swept across the course and made the exposed sections particularly demanding, with the CCLEX bridge providing one of the race’s biggest physical and tactical tests. Schoeman managed to hold his advantage through the bike and carried that cushion into the half-marathon, where the tropical heat turned the final leg into a test of patience and survival. “I just wanted to make sure that I get to the finish line, because I know it gets really hot on the run,” he said. Schoeman, who had split times of 27:23 (swim)-2:10:09 (bike)-1:26:15 (run), revealed that cramps forced him to ease off his pace, opting to race conservatively rather than risk losing the victory in the closing kilometers. He held off Austrian Sebastian Fuchs and Ben Hamilton of New Zealand, who clocked 4:12:51 (35:33-2:09:36-1:22:19) and 4:14:34 (32:34-2:10:01-1:27:06), respectively. While Schoeman celebrated a triumphant return, Australian Olympian Natalie Van Coevorden delivered an equally impressive performance, capturing the women’s professional crown in the race organized by Sunrise Events, Inc., which drew more than 1,400 triathletes from 48 countries, with the majority competing for top honors in various age-group divisions. The huge turnout also underscored how the IRONMAN 70.3 Lapu-Lapu has become a regular and much-anticipated part of Cebu’s sporting calendar – a race where elite international competition, challenging tropical conditions and the unmistakable energy of the Cebuano crowd come together year after year. As in previous editions, thousands of spectators lined the course, turning the roads and finish area into a wall of sound that helped carry exhausted athletes through the most challenging portions of the race. Their boisterous support has also become one of the defining features of IRONMAN racing in Cebu. Van Coevorden clocked 4:30:11 to dominate an all-Australian podium, finishing ahead of compatriots Charlotte McShane, who posted 4:47:33, and Paige Cranage, who crossed the finish line in 4:53:17. Van Coevorden, who competed in both the women’s individual and mixed relay events at the 2024 Paris Olympics, admitted the conditions were among the toughest she had experienced in a 70.3 race. The heat was relentless, the wind was persistent and, for much of the day, she found herself racing alone at the front. “I think we had probably the most challenging conditions I've ever had for a 70.3 today. It was hot, it was windy, and I had a pretty solo day by myself,” she said, visibly relieved after securing the victory. The swim proved especially difficult, with the strong current making the return leg particularly demanding. Van Coevorden also had to contend with the wind on the bike, recalling how she feared being blown toward the water while crossing the bridge, but maintained her rhythm and stayed within herself. McShane, who battled Van Coevorden near the front early on, said the swim took a heavy toll. A strong current helped propel the athletes outward, but the return trip became a brutal fight against the water, leaving her depleted before she even reached the bike. “I felt pretty terrible straight away on the bike,” said McShane, describing the remainder of the race as survival. The wind added another layer of difficulty, while the heat made the run equally unforgiving as the professionals battled simply to keep moving toward the finish. Austria’s 24-year-old rising star Fuchs, meanwhile, turned in the biggest result of his young career with a strong runner-up finish, drawing strength from a deeply personal motivation. “Four years ago my dad died and this is for him,” he said, dedicating the performance to his father. Fuchs said the swim was particularly rough and choppy, while the bike demanded plenty of strength on the bridge and the uphill sections. By the run, the heat had intensified the suffering, but the massive Cebu crowd gave him and the other athletes a much-needed lift. “The crowd was amazing and they pushed us so hard,” he said. That boisterous support has become one of the defining features of IRONMAN racing in Cebu. As in previous editions, thousands of spectators lined the course, turning the roads and finish area into a wall of sound that helped carry exhausted athletes through the most painful portions of the race.

Tagaytay to host inaugural Asian Youth Plus track tilt. Tagaytay City will host the inaugural Asian Youth Plus Track Championships next year at the Tagaytay CT Velodrome, according to Philippine Olympic Committee (POC) president Abraham “Bambol” Tolentino. The new continental championships for track cyclists aged 16 and below, Tolentino said, was approved during the Asian Cycling Confederation (ACC) Management Committee Meeting held in Kuala Lumpur over the weekend. “The Asian Youth Plus Track Championships aims to provide a platform to develop young cyclists in the whole of Asia with an expanded scope including Oceania,” Tolentino said. It will enable young Asian cyclists to compete against a broader international field and further raising the standard of competition.” The POC president said the dates of the track championships will be announced soon. They unpack how chauvinist politics – defined as a combination of imperialism, sexism and autocracy – have shaped Russian society and politics under President Vladimir Putin and helped pave the way for Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. CONFERENCE LEAGUE :POSSIBILE 0-3 A TAVOLINO PER LA FIORENTINA. I TIFOSI VIOLA CI SPERANO!!!. Gli otto punti rimediati da Cristiano Biraghi in finale di Conference League contro il West Ham hanno fatto molto discutere, non soltanto per il gesto vergognoso. Tra le questioni affrontate anche quella dell’interruzione della partita e del 3-0 a tavolino, provvedimenti su cui l’arbitro Del Cerro Grande, da norma, non può nulla. È la Commissione Disciplinare Uefa a decidere. Andiamo quindi a spulciare il regolamento. Tra i casi in cui i club devono rispondere delle azioni della tifoseria c’è anche “il lancio di oggetti che possa mettere in pericolo l’integrità fisica di altri presenti alla partita o pregiudicarne lo svolgimento”. Il paradosso è che Biraghi, per sperare in un 3-0 a tavolino, avrebbe dovuto accentuare il dolore e farsi sostituire, invece è stato “colpevole” di essersi grintosamente rialzato. Per dare un’idea del modo in cui viene messo in pratica il regolamento, prendiamo in esame un caso simile: il famoso petardo in testa a Dida nel derby di Milano del 2004-2005. In quel caso le autorità capiscono che la situazione non può avere seguito e inoltre il brasiliano resta a terra. Per questo motivo, viene assegnato il 3-0 a tavolino ai rossoneri. In sostanza, il West Ham al momento rischia solo una pesante sanzione pecuniaria e la squalifica del campo nella prossima edizione dell’Europa League. Un caso simile, alla Fiorentina , è capitato nella stessa competizione contro il Sivasspor, in Turchia. Alessandro Bianco riceve un pugno in faccia da un invasore di campo della squadra di casa. Il calciatore rimedia la frattura del setto nasale. Per i turchi è arrivata una dura sanzione, più l’impossibilità di andare allo stadio per una giornata per i tifosi.

LAGIORNATA MONDIALE DELLE TARTARUGHE MARINE. Sono già una dozzina i nidi censiti dal network tartarughe marine del WWF in Sicilia (proprio in queste ore sono in corso le operazioni di verifica e messa in sicurezza degli ultimi), e uno in Calabria. Il Mediterraneo, sebbene rappresenti solo una piccola percentuale della superficie totale degli oceani, lo 0.82%, ospita una straordinaria varietà di vita marina. Con oltre 17.000 specie diverse, questa regione è un importante hotspot di biodiversità marina. E tra questa vasta varietà di specie, le tartarughe marine occupano un posto speciale. Nel Mediterraneo, tre specie di tartarughe marine hanno fatto di queste acque la loro casa: la tartaruga comune (Caretta caretta, l’unica che vi si riproduce), la tartaruga verde (Chelonia mydas) e la tartaruga liuto (Dermochelys coriacea). Le tartarughe marine trascorrono la maggior parte della loro vita in mare, ma, come altri rettili, respirano aria tramite i polmoni. La deposizione delle uova è l’unica fase vitale che avviene sulla terraferma, di solito tra maggio e agosto nel Mediterraneo. Dopo l’accoppiamento, le femmine raggiungono la spiaggia per deporre le uova, che vengono incubate dal calore del sole (e del suolo) per circa due mesi. La temperatura influisce anche sul sesso delle tartarughe neonate: temperature superiori a 29°C tendono a produrre femmine, mentre temperature inferiori generano maschi. Dopo la deposizione delle uova, le femmine ritornano alle loro zone di alimentazione, che possono trovarsi anche a migliaia di chilometri di distanza dalle zone di riproduzione. Una volta raggiunta la maturità sessuale, intorno ai 20-30 anni, le tartarughe ritornano alle stesse aree di riproduzione per deporre le uova. La loro capacità di orientarsi durante queste lunghe migrazioni è influenzata dall’incredibile abilità di percepire il campo geomagnetico terrestre, una sorta di sesto senso di queste antichissime specie. L’impatto dei cambiamenti climatici. L’aumento delle temperature globali influisce direttamente sull’habitat di queste creature e sulle risorse di cui dipendono per la loro sopravvivenza, oltre che sulle correnti. Uno degli effetti più evidenti è l’aumento della temperatura dell’acqua. Le tartarughe marine sono specie ectotermiche, il che significa che la loro temperatura corporea dipende dall’ambiente circostante. Con l’aumento delle temperature marine, le tartarughe possono trovarsi in situazioni di stress termico, poiché non sono in grado di regolare la propria temperatura interna. Questo può influire sul loro metabolismo, sulla loro capacità di digerire il cibo e sull’efficienza riproduttiva.

TERRORE IN ASPROMONTE:AVVISTATI OMINI VERDI. Sono tante le domande in merito: si è trattato di extraterrestri? Di una qualche antica razza di ominidi ) sfuggita all’evoluzione? Il mostro – ha assicurato il tizio sotto shock – scorrazzava per i monti con fare minaccioso azzannando tutto ciò che si muoveva. Questo ci ha spinto, però, ad avviare un’indagine con tanto di sopralluogo nel perimetro interessato. Quello che abbiamo scoperto ha dell’incredibile! Non poche sono state infatti le persone (soggetti attendibilissimi) che (mettendo da parte la storia del mostro) hanno dichiarato di essersi imbattuti, nel corso degli anni e durante i periodi dei lavori di campagna, con dei piccoli omini verdi. Esseri buffi – secondo loro – non più alti del metro e venti, piuttosto schivi, che si aggirano furtivamente per le campagne di Stole, ma anche di Varet e di Campolaco. Come detto, sono molte le testimonianze in tal senso. BONUS VACANZE: SCADENZA DELLE DOMANDE IL 30 GIUGNO. La procedura per la richiesta del Bonus vacanze va effettuata solamente online tramite la app “Io” da smartphone. Basta munirsi di Spid o della carta d’identità elettronica. Lo possono richiedere soltanto i nuclei familiari con un reddito Isee sotto i 40.000 euro e può essere speso solo per un soggiorno in Italia entro la fine dell’anno. Una volta ottenuto il Bonus, la prenotazione della vacanza non può essere effettuata su siti online: quindi non è possibile prenotare né con Booking né con Airbnb o con altri siti di prenotazione. Bisogna, invece, prenotare tramite agenzie viaggi o o tour operator tradizionali o direttamente con la struttura scelta nella meta di villeggiatura. Ecco gli step per fare la richiesta del Bonus vacanze: se non si è già scaricata la app “Io” in passato sul proprio smartphone è possibile farlo sia per telefoni Apple sia per Android; la prima volta che si scarica la app viene richiesta la registrazione che è possibile fare più facilmente digitando un Pin a scelta o, per chi è più pratico, attraverso il riconoscimento biometrico (impronta digitale o riconoscimento del volto); una volta entrati nella app, bisogna selezionare la sezione “pagamenti” e quindi il Bonus vacanze; a questo punto è necessario inserire le informazioni richieste, tra cui il valore dell’Isee; se tutte le informazioni inserite sono corrette, la app genera un codice associato al vostro Bonus vacanze con un QrCode; sia il codice sia il QrCode devono essere mostrati alla struttura al momento del pagamento. N.B. Prima di effettuare la richiesta del Bonus vacanze è bene tenere sotto mano sia la propria identità Spid sia la carta d’identità elettronica e i dati del proprio Isee (chi non lo ricorda può recuperarlo all’Inps o al proprio Caf). Il Bonus di un valore massimo di 500 euro è rivolto alle famiglie italiane composte da almeno tre persone. Per i nuclei familiari composti da due persone il Bonus vacanze scende a 300 euro, ma lo possono ottenere anche i single, in questo caso il valore è di 150 euro.
